page1.text:
It was a beautiful, moonlit night.
I was just enjoying the sight with my father, Kiritsugu Emiya.
It was winter, but it wasn't very cold.
On the veranda it was just a little chilly, the perfect weather to watch the moon.

page2.text:
Kiritsugu didn't go outside much anymore.
He rarely went out, and he spent most of his time lounging around the house.
...Every time I recall this, I still feel regret.
Why didn't I realize that he was acting the way any creature does when they know their time is almost up?

page3.text:
"When I was a boy, I wanted to be a champion of justice."
He blurted it out, just out of nowhere.
My father, who already seemed like a champion of justice in my eyes, said that as if he were reflecting on a memory.

page4.text:
"What, you wanted to? So you gave up on it?"
I asked, unable to completely hide my disappointment.
Kiritsugu smiled apologetically, and looked up at the distant moon.

page5.text:
"Unfortunately, yes. You can only be a hero for so long. It gets harder to call yourself one as you grow up. I wish I'd found that out earlier."
That made sense to me.
I wasn't sure why, but if Kiritsugu said it, then it had to be true.

page6.text:
"Oh. Well, that's too bad."
"Yes. It really is too bad."
Kiritsugu nodded in agreement.
So I just kind of blurted something out, as if it were a natural thing to say.

page7.text:
"Okay. If you can't do it, then I'll do it for you.
You can't do anything because you're an adult, but I can. You can leave your dream to me."

page8.text: Because I'll make it a reality.

page9.text:
The bold promise made my father smile.
His face said everything I needed to know.
Kiritsugu made a long, contented sigh, and whispered,
"Ah...that's a relief."
There, he closed his eyes, and so too his life came to a close.

page10.text:
He looked so peaceful, like he was just going to wake up in the morning, so I didn't think much about it.
Maybe it was because by then I was used to seeing death.
On a winter night, the man I called my father looked up at the moon and entered a long sleep.

page11.text:
The yard was dead silent...not so much as a single chirp from an insect.
I still remember how fiercely my eyes blazed on that brilliant, dark night.
I didn't cry out loud, nor did I feel sad.
But tears flowed down my cheek until the moon sank past the horizon.

page12.text:
This happened in the winter, five years ago.
I probably cried ten years' worth of tears in that time, so after that, there was nothing left.

page13.text:
Fuji-nee's dad took care of the funeral arrangements, and that's how I ended up living in the Emiya mansion all alone.
Kiritsugu's passing didn't change anything for me.
I was set on becoming a man who champions justice and does what's right, just like my father, so I didn't have time to sit around.

page14.text:
That's right.
I never talk about this, but I still remember it.
Ten years ago, a man saved me from a fire.
He picked up a burned, dying child and carried him out of hell, weeping with joy.

page15.text:
I've admired him ever since.
Nobody else saved me.
I couldn't save anyone.
In the ruins of the fire, there was only a boy who was saved, and the man who saved him.
That's why I aspired to be like him.

page16.text:
I wanted to become a hero of justice that saves people and doesn't let anyone die.
That's who he wanted to be, and he passed his wish on to me before quietly letting the curtain fall.

page17.text:
It's only natural for a child to follow in their father's footsteps.
Shirou Emiya must become a hero of justice and save someone the same way that he was once saved.
I swore to myself I would do it.
I vowed to fulfill the dream of the man I most admired.

page18.text:
...But honestly, I didn't know how.
What did Kiritsugu mean by doing the right thing and championing justice? How can I grow up faster? Is there some magical way to make Kiritsugu's dream of 'making everyone happy' come true? Seriously, what am I supposed do when I become a Master and I can't get the blonde girl with me out of my head—

page19.text:
"...rgh."
I wake up in my room.
"...Ugh...something tastes...terrible..."
The steely tang of blood clouds my mouth.
It pooled in my mouth while I slept, and every time I breathe, heavy, metallic air fills my lungs.

page20.text:
...
I'm not sure why I feel this way.
A violent urge to vomit makes me want to go wash my face in the restroom.

page21.text:
"Okay."
I lift myself out of bed.
Dizziness sets my head spinning.
Feeling uneasy on my feet, I plant a hand on the wall.
"...Ugh."
I try to move, but it only makes the nausea worse.
...No, it's more pain than nausea.

page22.text:
My body feels sluggish, and my insides seem to churn whenever I move. I imagine this is about what it'd feel like if someone forced hot lead down my throat.
"Ugh...imagining that is making me feel like I'm going to run a fever."
I wipe the sweat from my forehead and hobble out of my room, leaning against the wall.

page23.text:
"Okay, I feel a little better."
I wash my face and dry off my sweat-drenched body.
"...Huh?"
For some reason, my abdomen is wrapped in bandages.
I have no idea why, but I'll deal with it later.

page24.text:
"...I'm hungry. Did I leave any extra food in the fridge...?"
My stomach still feels like it's churning, but my body needs nourishment.

page25.text:
"Kngh..."
I suck up the discomfort and keep walking, braced against the wall.
The dizziness won't go away, and worst of all, my whole body feels dull.
"Ow! Ow, ow..."
I keep moving forward, making pathetic noises along the way.
What the hell did I do before I went to bed last night?
I don't remember training strenuously enough to make my entire body ache.

page26.text:
I reach the living room.
Sakura and Fuji-nee must be at school.
There's no signs of breakfast, nor do I see any remnants of Fuji-nee wrecking the place.
The living room's quiet, like a typical Sunday—
"Morning. Sorry I came in without asking, Emiya."
...or not.

page27.text:
"Wha... Eh!?"
Rin Tohsaka is sitting on the floor by the table in the living room.
She's so calm, like she owns the place. So much so that I feel like the guest here.

page28.text:
"..."
I have no idea what to say, so I plop down on a cushion.
And then I take a deep breath.

page29.text:
"Tohsaka, why're you—"
"Stop. Shouldn't you apologize to me first? I can't move on from last night until you say sorry for what you did."
...I can't even finish asking why she's in my house.

page30.text:
Tohsaka's glare is all I need to know how angry she is.
She seems upset about something that happened last night, but what exactly...

page31.text:
"Wait."
Now I remember.
Right, this isn't the time for me to be leisurely breathing in the morning air.
I tried to help Saber, and... Berserker gutted me like a fish.

page32.text:
"...Ugh."
The nausea returns.
A chill grips my entire body as I remember the feeling of having a gaping hole in my body.

page33.text:
Wait, that's weird.
I should've died instantly.

page34.text:
"That's weird. Why am I still here?"
"Do you remember now? You did something damned stupid last night. I hope you regret it."

page35.text:
Tohsaka huffs critically.
That kinda ticks me off.
My brain, frozen since seeing Tohsaka in my living room, finally grinds into action.

page36.text:
"What are you talking about? I had no choice. Well, sure...it might seem like an idiotic move if you just look at the results...and I definitely meant for it to go better than it did...
So I wouldn't say it was a mistake."
I return her glare, insisting that I'm not an idiot.

page37.text:
"...Mrgh."
Wh-what?
Why is she making such a show of sighing tiredly at me?

page38.text: "If the Master dies, the Servant disappears too, remember? I can't believe you actually tried to shield your own Servant."

page39.text:
"Listen. If you die, then Saber is gone, too. If you wanted to save Saber, you should have thought of another way to do it from a safe distance.
...Honestly, do you realize how pointless it is to risk your own life for your Servant's?"

page40.text:
"I wasn't shielding her. I was just trying to get her out of there. I didn't think that would happen to me."
I knew I might die if I got near a monster like that, but that's beside the point.

page41.text:
"...Fine. Then you had the wrong idea."
Tohsaka only looks more irritated, like she knows exactly what I'm thinking.

page42.text:
"I'll be straight with you, Emiya. I didn't take you to the church so that you could win.
I was just trying to give you a chance to survive because you literally don't know anything. It sounds like you still don't get it."

page43.text:
"A chance to survive...?"
"Yeah. I figured you wouldn't take risks or really do much if you knew defeat meant death. But it looks like you're the kind of person to go out at night even in a situation like this.
I thought that if I scared you straight, you wouldn't throw your own life away for someone else, and if you're lucky, you'd make it until the end."

page44.text:
"I see. That didn't cross my mind."
So that's why she's so unhappy at me for facing down Berserker.

page45.text: "But why are you upset? What does me dying have to do with you?"

page46.text: "It has everything to do with me, because you made me worry all night long!"

page47.text:
Tohsaka is practically throwing a tantrum.
...But, okay.
It actually feels good to have someone worry about me.
From her tone, it sounds like Tohsaka was the one who took care of me.

page48.text:
"Is that so? Guess I owe you one, Tohsaka. Thanks."
I bow my head in appreciation and apology.
...

page49.text: "Hmph! As long as you understand. If you've learned your lesson, then use your head next time."

page50.text:
Tohsaka quickly turns away.
She might still be edgy, but I feel like she's in a better mood.

page51.text:
"Then we're done with what happened last night.
Let's get down to it, then. Do you want to talk business, or talk about yesterday?"

page52.text:
"Hm?"
Tohsaka prompts me matter-of-factly.
Her straightforwardness takes me off guard, but now that I think about it, she must be here only because she has something to discuss.

page53.text:
If she hadn't had something to discuss, she'd have gone home already.
Tohsaka's my enemy, so what could she have to talk about that would prompt her to stay in enemy territory?

page54.text:
I'm curious to know what she's thinking, and I also want to know what else happened last night.
I have to ask anyway, so...

page55.text:
"Let's start with what happened last night."
"Yeah, you should know what's going on first. Hey, looks like you're finally thinking straight."
With a smug grin, Tohsaka launches into a brief explanation of last night's events.

page56.text:
Apparently, Berserker left right after I lost consciousness.
Afterwards, my body started to heal on its own, and was back to normal after a few minutes.
I was still unconscious, so Tohsaka brought me here and the rest was as I remember it.

page57.text:
"What's important here is that you managed to survive on your own. I might have helped a bit, but it was your power that healed your wound. So, don't get that twisted, okay?"
"That's what it sounds like from the way you told it. So you aren't the one who healed me?"

page58.text: "No way. I can't revive someone on the verge of death. What was I supposed to do about your intestines scattered on the pavement?"

page59.text:
"...Hm."
I don't really have an answer to that.
My stomach is back to normal, yes, but I'm honestly still dubious about what Tohsaka said.
I can't even use any healing magecraft, much less raise the dead.

page60.text:
"Which means it must be your Servant.
Either your Servant is pretty powerful, or something happened when you summoned them... I think it's both, actually, but you must be connected by some line."

page61.text: "Line? You mean some sort of fated line that connects a familiar and its mage?"

page62.text:
"Oh, so you do have some knowledge of familiars.
Then this should be easy: it means your relationship with Saber is not just an ordinary Master and familiar relationship."

page63.text:
"Saber can evidently regenerate too, so her power might be flowing into you.
Normally the mage's abilities are shared with their familiar, but in your case, the familiar's abilities are helping the Master."

page64.text:
"Hm. So it's like a river flowing upstream?"
"That's a good way of putting it. Normally, that wouldn't be possible, but Saber's magical energy must be powerful enough to change the flow of a river. Otherwise there's no chance she'd be able to go up against Berserker with that tiny frame of hers."

page65.text:
"It wouldn't normally be possible... Does that mean your relationship with Archer is a normal mage and familiar relationship?"
"That's right. He doesn't listen to a word I say, but that's our relationship."

page66.text:
"The connection between Master and Servant is like gas and an engine. We provide the energy for them to consume.
...Though, I've read that a Master once acquired pseudo-immortality by physically fusing with their Servant. They wouldn't die as long as their Servant doesn't die... Are you listening, Emiya?"

page67.text:
"Huh...? Yeah, I am.
Then, Tohsaka, does that mean my body will heal from injuries even if I don't do anything about them?"

page68.text:
"At the cost of your Servant's magical energy. I don't know how it works, but it definitely has something to do with Saber being stuck in material form. I don't think you've learned any curses of natural regeneration."
"Of course not. My old man never taught me something that complicated."

page69.text: "That's not what I mean. I'm saying I wouldn't have had to worry this much if it was true. Never mind, this doesn't concern you."

page70.text:
Huh?
What does she mean?
I wonder why Tohsaka's being so roundabout.

page71.text:
"Anyway, just don't do anything rash.
You might have survived this time, but you might not live to tell the tale next time you get hurt like last night. It's probably best you just ditch the notion that any small wounds will heal on their own."

page72.text: "I know. Saber had to help me because I went and got myself hurt. I don't have any excuses for that."

page73.text:
"That's not the point, dummy. Let me be clear: it costs more than Saber's magical energy to heal your wounds.
You're giving something up when it happens.
Whether that's your life, your luck, or even your bank account, you can bet that kind of healing doesn't come cheap."
Tohsaka huffs once again.
And I agree, but...

page74.text:
"Tohsaka. I don't think my bank account has anything to do with it."
"Of course it does! Using magecraft means you're pretty much throwing your money away. The more you use it, the more it drains your money!
Otherwise none of this would be acceptable! Especially to me!"
Tohsaka absolutely explodes with fury.

page75.text:
It's odd, really.
The more I talk to her, the more this Tohsaka feels like the real one, while the girl at school feels like an act.
...Though, I guess I already noticed that yesterday.

page76.text:
"Well, putting the topic of money aside...
I want to talk about something serious. Are you ready, Emiya?"
"It's the main reason you're here, isn't it? Let's hear it."

page77.text:
"Then I'll be frank. What do you plan to do next?"
Tohsaka asks the one question I hoped she wouldn't.

page78.text:
...Actually, that's not entirely true.
It's not that I don't want her to ask so much as...I haven't really thought of my answer yet.
What am I going to do now... It's the question I want to ask.

page79.text:
"...To be honest, I don't know. I know there's a competition for the Holy Grail, but I've never been in a battle between mages.
For one thing, I..."
More than anything, I want to avoid any killing.

page80.text:
"I'm not interested in something like the Holy Grail.
I don't really know if I can risk my life for something I don't want."
"I knew you'd say something like that. I'll have you know that your Servant will kill you for saying that sort of thing."

page81.text:
"Wha...kill me!? Why?"
"Because the Servants also seek the Holy Grail.
One of the conditions for them allowing a Master to summon them is getting a chance at the Holy Grail."

page82.text:
"The Grail is the Servants' number one priority.
They'll obey the Masters if it gives them a chance at the Grail, and sometimes they'll even die for their Masters.
Try saying you don't want the Grail to your Servant. You can't blame her if she calls you a traitor and cuts you down where you stand."

page83.text:
"What the hell? That doesn't sound right. Servants are the ones who're summoned by Masters, right?
Then..."

page84.text:
"Did you think Servants would really serve humans for free?
Whoever acquires the Grail gets their wish granted, whether that's a Master or their guardian Servant.
The Servants have wishes of their own. That's why they respond to summons that would otherwise be, at best, unreasonable."

page85.text:
"Masters don't summon Servants to help them get the Holy Grail.
Servants answer the Masters' call to have a chance at the Holy Grail."

page86.text:
...
The Servants have wishes, too...?
Does that mean Saber also has a wish she wants granted by the Holy Grail?

page87.text:
"That's why Servants will go out and eliminate other Masters even without being ordered to. Only one person can get the Holy Grail. They won't allow it to fall into the hands of anyone other than their own Master.
Unlike Masters, Servants don't have the power to take away Command Spells. The only way they can neutralize other Masters is by killing them."

page88.text:
"So even if the Master has no intention of fighting, conflict is inevitable.
Masters attacked by a Servant need to fight them off with their own Servant. Kirei told you plenty of times about how that is at the heart of the Holy Grail War."

page89.text:
"Yeah, he told me enough of that last night.
But..."

page90.text:
That means that Servants must fight and kill each other.
I thought it would've been enough as long as the Masters made peace with each other and gave up the Holy Grail. But if Servants answer the summons because they also seek the Holy Grail and will never give up until they have it, then battle between Servants really is inevitable.
But then...
...is the girl who fought so hard to protect me also here to fight, kill for, and maybe die...all for the Holy Grail?

page91.text:
"...That's awful. I don't know exactly what a Heroic Spirit is, but Saber's human. I even saw her bleed yesterday."
"Oh, don't worry about that. Servants aren't mortal, so if they die, they'll just go back to where they came from. Heroic Spirits are phenomena that can't die. Only Masters can actually get killed when they lose a fight."

page92.text:
"No, I mean..."
Even if their deaths are figurative...
It doesn't change the fact that something which takes the form of a human dies in this world.

page93.text:
"What, you have some hang-up with killing? You've got some nerve calling yourself a mage, with morals like that."
...

page94.text:
Tohsaka's right.
As a mage, death is never far.
I understand that fact, and I've long since resigned myself to it.
But I'm not strong enough to be the judge of when and where other people should live or die.

page95.text:
"Of course I do. I won't be party to some war where people murder each other."
"Oh really? So you're just going to sit and wait to be killed? You're going to just hand the victory to some other Master."

page96.text:
"That's not my point. All I have to do is to stay alive until the end, right? I don't intend to kill anyone, but I'm also not going to hold back if I need to defend myself.
...Someone who shows up ready to kill others can't complain about getting killed."

page97.text: "Hm. So you're going to play defense. You're just going to watch and see what the other Masters do? Even if that thing from yesterday goes around killing everyone in town, you'll just ignore it?"

page98.text:
The thing from yesterday?
That twisted, inhuman demon...
...
It's strong enough to level a house with a single blow.
...If it set its mind to it, I'm sure it could destroy all of Miyama overnight.

page99.text:
To make matters worse, Servants can turn into spirit form.
Humans who lack the ability to sense the supernatural can't even see them.
But as soon as Servants materialize, they can interact with the physical world. You could say they're the ultimate weapons.
No modern technology or weaponry can affect a spiritual form.

page100.text:
Our attacks don't work on them, but they can hurt us.
It's a depressingly one-sided arrangement.
From a normal person's point of view, Servants may as well be natural disasters.
When people die to an invisible killer, those deaths will just be treated as accidents or natural causes.

page101.text:
"What do you mean? Don't Servants—I mean, don't Masters and Servants only attack other Masters? What do the people in town have to do with it?"
"If only the world were so peaceful. If that was the case, then we wouldn't need Kirei to play referee."

page102.text:
"I should have mentioned this sooner, but Servants are spirits. Their forms are complete, static, so they do not grow.
But they still need magical energy as fuel.
When they are provided with more magical energy, they are able to use more of the special abilities they had while they were alive.
That's not unlike us mages, actually... Do you see what I'm getting at?"

page104.text:
Magical energy is like gunpowder; the mage is the gun itself.
Like how there are different guns—pistols, rifles, shotguns— mages all have a variety of abilities.
To continue the metaphor, Servants are more like artillery cannons than firearms.
They burn a huge amount of gunpowder to launch massive shells.

page105.text:
"That's right. But Servants can't draw mana from the atmosphere like us. They generally run only on the magical energy within them.
It's our job as Masters to supplement that energy. Their power is limited by their own energy supply, plus whatever their Masters give them."

page106.text:
"That means a half-baked Master like you has no chance against a more capable Master, right?
One very obvious solution to that hurdle is to have your Servant acquire magical energy from other sources.
Servants are spirits, so they can eat similar stuff for sustenance."

page107.text:
"Hm?"
Eating something similar...?
"You mean other spiritual bodies? But what kind of spirits would they eat?"

page108.text:
"Simple. Spirits of nature can take in power from nature itself.
So what do you think Servants, who are human spirits, get power from?"
"Oh..."
It really is an easy question.
Just as we eat meat, human spirits like Servants have to eat...

page109.text:
"Correct. To be fair, the magical energy supply from Masters chosen by the Holy Grail should be enough in most cases.
But shouldn't it be obvious that they'd gain more energy by getting it from more than one person?
Bluntly speaking, inferior Masters have to feed other people to their Servants."
...

page110.text:
"Servants can convert souls and primal human emotions into magical energy.
If you want your Servant to get stronger, that's the most efficient way. It's not rare for Masters to sacrifice humans to their Servant."

page111.text:
"Sacrifice... Are you saying there might be Masters out there who go around killing people to make their Servants stronger, if they're not choosy about their methods?"
"Maybe. But I can't see a smart Master doing something like that."

page112.text:
"No matter how strong a Servant is, they're still limited by energy capacity. They can't store any energy above a hard limit, so there's only so much they can benefit from mass murder.
For one thing, the Association won't just turn a blind eye to someone going around murdering people, but more importantly, the other Masters will be able to figure out the Servant's abilities and identity based on the victims' cause of death. That, and they'll work out the other Master's identity too.
Concealing your identity in a Holy Grail war gives you a big advantage, so any normal Master would be unwilling to use their Servant."

page113.text:
...I get it.
If you don't let anyone know you're a Master, then the other Masters won't attack you.
Conversely, if the other Masters know who you are, you're just asking to be ambushed.
It stands to reason that no one would be reckless enough to let their Servant attack civilians and risk getting exposed.

page114.text: "Well that's a relief. As long as a Master doesn't order it, Servants shouldn't indiscriminately attack people."

page115.text:
"Probably not. They're supposed to be heroes, after all. I don't think there are any heroes who'd attack innocent people... though I can't say that for sure.
Plenty of them became heroes through sheer violence."

page116.text:
"..."
Tohsaka just casually raises a truly terrifying point.
That she sounds genuine about it, rather than sarcastic or ironic, might be a reflection of her twisted nature.

page117.text:
"We're getting off topic. So, what's next for you?
You claim you won't kill people, so are you just going to stand by and watch the other Masters do god knows what?"

page118.text:
...I take it back.
She's not only twisted, she's a jerk who's going out of her way to drive me into a corner, all with a smile.

page119.text:
"If it comes to that, I'll go in to stop them. The Master won't have much to do as long as their Servant has been defeated, right?"
"Unbelievable. So you're not going to try to defeat any of the other Masters, unless they intend to do bad things.
Do you even hear yourself?"

page120.text: "Yeah. I know they're just pretty words. But I can't think of anything else. I'm not changing my principles, no matter what you say."

page121.text:
"Hmm. There's just one problem. Should I spell it out for you?"
I can see the gears turning in her head. She's up to something.
But I promised to listen, so I need to hear her out.

page122.text:
"Y-yeah?"
"Do you remember the Master from yesterday? The little girl who just casually ordered her Servant to kill us both?"
...
How can I forget? She attacked us on our way home without any warning.

page123.text:
"She is definitely going to come back and kill us. I'm sure even you've worked that out."
...
Oh...right.
That girl's a Master too.

page124.text:
She knows that Tohsaka and I are both Masters, so she's bound to come after us eventually.
It could be today or tomorrow, but we've already signed our death warrants.
I have no chance of stopping that monster.

page125.text:
"Her Servant, Berserker, is on a whole other level.
As inexperienced of a Master as you are, you're no match for that thing. And you've been saying you're going to protect yourself by doing nothing. You are not going to be able to defend yourself."

page126.text: "Look who's talking. You have no chance against that thing either."

page127.text: "Not in a straight-up fight. That's the ultimate close-quarters Servant. There probably isn't anyone who can match it even among all the heroes of myth and legend. If Berserker attacks me, there's no escape."

page128.text: "...That goes for me, too. I'm pretty sure I won't survive the next round with that thing."

page129.text:
My hand moves unconsciously to my stomach.
The wound is closed.
It's probably not even fair to call this a wound. It's the spot where a gigantic sword nearly killed me instantly.
I can't shake off the sudden wave of nausea that wells up in me when I imagine the next time I might get a taste of that blade.

page130.text: "There you have it. Do you get that just sitting around, doing nothing and waiting for the Holy Grail War to end isn't an option?"

page131.text:
"...Yeah, I know that now. But Tohsaka, I'm not sure what your point is.
I'm sure you're not here just to make fun of my inevitable doom...are you?"

page132.text:
"What kind of sadist do you take me for!?
After everything I said, you still can't take a hint? I'm asking if you want to team up."

page133.text:
"Hm?"
Hm? Wuh? What now? Uh...what?
If I take those words at face value, that means...

page134.text:
"Y-you want to team up with me, Tohsaka!?"
"Yeah. My Archer's still recovering from a serious wound. That's going to take some time, but in the meantime, I'm not completely out of the fight.
And while your Servant is superb, her Master's dragging her down, making her half as effective. See? Put the two of us together and you've got a whole."

page135.text:
"Hey, I'm not that bad of a mage."
"I count three times in which you almost died. You're the first person I know who's had that happen in a single day."

page136.text:
"Urgh. But..."
"I'll make it worth your while. I'll let you off for getting Archer hurt, and teach you what you need to know to be a Master. Oh, and if we have time, I can even give you some pointers on your magecraft. Deal?"

page137.text:
Ugh.
It is an attractive proposition.
I know next to nothing, and Tohsaka does seem knowledgeable.

page138.text: And I'd like to avoid fighting her, if I can.
